en.purpose: To classify breast cancer using the pathological TNM system by recording pT, pN, and pM categories and to determine the corresponding AJCC/UICC anatomic stage group.
en.use:
Use this guideline to record pathological TNM (pT, pN, pM) for breast cancer and to derive a pathological stage group (0, IA, IB, IIA, IIB, IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IV) based on pTNM combinations.

Inputs
- pT Primary tumor (pTX, pT0, pTis, pT1-pT4) and optional pT subcategories (pTis subcategory, pT1 subcategory, pT4 subcategory)
- pN Regional lymph nodes (pNX, pN0, pN0(i+), pN1-pN3) and optional pN subcategories (pN1 subcategory, pN2 subcategory, pN3 subcategory)
- pM Distant metastasis (pM0, pM1)

Outputs
- Pathological stage group (0, IA, IB, IIA, IIB, IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IV) derived from pT/pN/pM
- Pathological TNM assessment (e.g., pT2pN1pM0) and, where applicable, an additional output including selected subcategories (e.g., pT1cpN2apM0).

Key differences from clinical staging:
- Stage IB is assigned when pT0 or pT1 is combined with pN1mi (micrometastases) and pM0.
- pN0(i+) (isolated tumor cells) is treated as pN0 for staging purposes.
- pN1 subcategories (pN1mi, pN1a, pN1b, pN1c) are available for more detailed classification.
en.misuse: Not to be used for recording clinical TNM classification - use the clinical TNM guideline for that purpose. Not to be used for TNM classification of cancers outside the breast.

other_details.references: Brierley JD, Gospodarowicz MK, Wittekind C, editors. TNM classification of malignant tumours. 8th ed. Hoboken (NJ): Wiley Blackwell; 2017
other_details.en: A structured guideline used to determine the pathological TNM (Tumour-Node-Metastasis) classification and stage grouping for breast cancer according to the UICC/AJCC TNM system.
